floorPlan.note: Aligned to user-marked ZONE_FLOOR (SketchUp face painted with ZONE_FLOOR material). Origin = its min corner. Zones extracted via tools/glb-prep/extract-zones.mjs.
floorPlan.offsetNote: Re-verified against the 15:09, 18:03 and 19:47 re-imports: ZONE_FLOOR's min corner and its 4423x2544 bbox are bit-identical every time, so every saved project keeps its coordinates. This value must never move without a migration.
floorPlan.placeableAreas: 3 polygons (green) from ZONE_FLOOR; furniture is confined to these
floorPlan.note2: Real floor is non-rectangular & disconnected: left L + east rectangle + the new strip under the shortened passage.
floorPlan.note3: planSizeCm.width runs to 6051 because the raised reception deck (ZONE_KABALAT_PANIM, x 4432…6051, +470cm) shares this plan space. The hall alone is 4423 wide.

ceilingBeams.note: Lighting-truss grid, read off the 72 HalfCoupler clamps in the SKP (72 = 36 crossings × 2 = 9 × 4 × 2). The 19:47 SKP still carries 288 HalfCoupler nodes — the same 72 clamps × 4 parts (Bolt/Catch/M/Wingnut) — so the truss was not edited and the committed positions stand.
ceilingBeams.trussColorNote: baseColorFactor [0.725,0.635,0.533] with NO baseColor texture, so the factor is the colour. Use the sRGB form in code (three converts sRGB→linear and lands back on the glTF value); the linear hex would render too light. Identified two ways: every slender member at truss height carries this material, and exactly 9 of them (matching the 9-beam grid) pass through clamp crossings.

cameras.note: 7 SketchUp Scenes. Cameras do NOT survive the GLB export (inspect-cameras.mjs reports 0, which is correct and not a bug) — they are read from the SimLab session's Scene nodes and converted via (x, z, 24.861 − y). Values live in src/core/venuePacks.ts.
cameras.reverified: All 7 positions match the committed values to 4 decimals, and Scene 1's forward vector (0.8822,-0.4709,-0.0032) matches the committed position→target direction. Nothing to update.

source.skpModifiedNote: The user saved four times on 2026-07-28 (01:57, 15:09, 18:03, 19:47). This asset is built from the 19:47 save, which redrew ZONE_SAVIV and ZONE_POOL and extended the south-east floor strip. Every other figure here was re-measured on the 19:47 export and came out identical.
changesFromPreviousImport: ZONE_SAVIV REDRAWN. One face, 14 triangles, bbox x 766 y 1408 3196x1136 — but it paints only 72.20 m² of that box's 363.13 m² (19.9% fill). The true shape is a band around the water: two L strips, 123cm down each side and 203cm across the top, with a gap at x 1809…2579 where the two DJ pads sit. Four rectangles, not one. Its bounding box swallows the whole pool, which is the wrong surface the user reported seeing in the 2D plan.
ZONE_POOL REDRAWN to the water alone: one face, 10 triangles, bbox x 889 y 1611 2950x933, 87.1% fill — the water bitten out around the chuppah podium. Previously x 766 y 1408 3073x1136.
SAVIV now strictly CONTAINS POOL (it did not before), so saviv minus pool is exactly the ring. Expressible — but not as a single RestrictedZone rectangle.

floorAreas[2] pulled down to the south wall: x 3960…4420 now y 1410…2540, exact vertices x 3961.94…4422.51 by y 1407.57…2543.77 = 461x1136 (was reported 460x1080 off the 10cm raster of the older save). +2.3 m² of placeable floor.
outline is a plain rectangle again — [[0,0],[4420,0],[4420,2540],[0,2540]] — because that south-east notch closed.

UNCHANGED, all re-measured on this export: plan origin, size, wallHeight, hangHeight, ceilingBeams (288 HalfCoupler nodes = the same 72 clamps x 4 parts), all 7 cameras, truss colour, bar, dancefloor, both DJ faces, both chuppah faces, corridor, kabalatPanim.

THE RENDERED MODEL IS UNCHANGED. venue.glb rebuilt from the 19:47 save compares structurally identical to the 18:03 build: 9860 nodes, 351 meshes, 44 materials, 18 textures, 4438 primitives, 3217047 triangles, identical world bounds, and an identical per-material triangle distribution. Only the serialized bytes differ (Draco/buffer ordering is not deterministic); the file is even the same 5380184 bytes. glb-prep strips ZONE_* marker faces, so this is the proof that the user's 19:47 edits were confined entirely to the zone marker layers and touched no visible geometry.
notPastedIntoCode: ZONE_SAVIV and ZONE_POOL were NOT written into src/core/venuePacks.ts. They are one marker split in two, and the 18:03 pair still in the code covers x 766…3962 by y 1408…2544 — the complete no-go footprint. Narrowing pool to the water while saviv stays an 18:03 rectangle would uncover ~48.3 m² of pool apron and let furniture land on the pool edge the user explicitly painted. Both halves land together in PLAN-06, which also has to clamp to the NEAREST rectangle. Full geometry in Plans/R2/handoff/01c-venue-data.md.
notImported: A SECOND ZONE_DJ marker exists at x 1809 y 1408 (310×243), 460cm left of the committed one. Two rects cannot share a `kind`, so the committed position was kept. See BLOCKED-01-A1.md §2.

A SECOND ZONE_HUPA marker exists on the reception deck at x 4706 y 2009 (571×426, elevation 520 = deck 470 + the same 50cm riser as the hall chuppah). Not added, for the same reason. See BLOCKED-01-A1.md §3.
source.notDone: Source doc §6 (move the wall behind the bar back ≥2m) is STILL not in this asset — ZONE_BAR came out unchanged again on the 19:47 export. The user closed this as answered rather than as a model change: see Plans/R2/handoff/ANSWERS-WAVE-1.md §1, which confirms the wall sits at y=0 by design and the bar unit stands 1.20m in front of it. toolFixes: extract-zones.mjs now bounds one rect per marker FACE and merges only overlapping faces. Bounding all triangles of a material together turned the two ZONE_HUPA faces into a bogus 3468×784 rectangle spanning the gap, and aborted the run on a ZONE_HUPA/ZONE_CHUPPAH 'disagreement' that was really just a second marker.

extract-zones.mjs now labels solid cells with 4-connectivity before tracing contours. The new floor area touches the east strip at a single corner; the one-edge-per-corner map dropped an edge there and produced a loop cutting diagonally across the hall (1.47 m² instead of 2.43 m²). Verified: the two pre-existing floorAreas polygons now come out byte-identical to the committed values.
